blocks.content: Instructions: Select the single best answer. Answers are provided at the end.
Section A — History, Polity & Governance (Q1–Q35)

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Section A includes 35 multiple-choice questions focusing on History, Polity & Governance.
Section B features 35 multiple-choice questions dedicated to Geography, Biodiversity & Environment.
Section C covers 30 multiple-choice questions testing knowledge on Economy, Culture & Current Affairs.

blocks.content: 1. Tripura became a full state of India on:
(a) 9 September 1949  (b) 21 January 1972  (c) 20 February 1987  (d) 15 August 1972
2. Tripura merged with India (signed Merger Agreement) on:
(a) 15 August 1947  (b) 26 January 1950  (c) 9 September 1949  (d) 21 January 1949
3. The ruling dynasty of the Kingdom of Tripura was called:
(a) Chola  (b) Ahom  (c) Manikya  (d) Barua
4. Who was the last Maharaja of Tripura?
(a) Bir Chandra Manikya  (b) Bir Bikram Kishore Manikya  (c) Kirit Bikram Kishore Manikya  (d) Radha Kishore Manikya
5. Which Maharaja of Tripura introduced the first printing press in northeast India (1870)?
(a) Radha Kishore Manikya  (b) Bir Chandra Manikya  (c) Krishna Manikya  (d) Dhanya Manikya
6. The royal chronicle of Tripura's Manikya dynasty is called:
(a) Tripura Granth  (b) Manikya Purana  (c) Rajmala  (d) Tripura Itihaas
7. Unakoti rock carvings are located in which district:
(a) North Tripura  (b) South Tripura  (c) Unokoti district  (d) Dhalai
8. The Chaturdasha Devata (14 gods) festival of Tripura is called:
(a) Garia Puja  (b) Ker Puja  (c) Kharchi Puja  (d) Durga Puja
9. Kharchi Puja is held at which location:
(a) Agartala (New City area)  (b) Old Agartala (Purana Agartala) — Chaturdasha Devata Temple  (c) Udaipur  (d) Dharmanagar
10. Tripura Tribal Areas Autonomous District Council (TTAADC) was established under which Schedule of the Indian Constitution:
(a) Fifth Schedule  (b) Sixth Schedule  (c) Seventh Schedule  (d) Ninth Schedule
11. The TTAADC covers what percentage of Tripura's geographical area:

(a) Indian National Congress  (b) CPI  (c) CPI(M)-led Left Front  (d) BJP
13. Manik Sarkar, the iconic CM of Tripura, served for how long:
(a) 10 years  (b) 15 years  (c) 18 years  (d) 20 years (1998–2018)
14. BJP won Tripura in the historic 2018 election with how many seats:
15. TIPRA Motha, the new tribal party, was founded by:
(a) Manik Sarkar  (b) Biplab Kumar Deb  (c) Pradyot Kishore Manikya Debbarman  (d) Kirit Bikram Kishore
16. The current Chief Minister of Tripura (2024) is:
(a) Biplab Kumar Deb  (b) Manik Sarkar  (c) Manik Saha  (d) Pradyot Kishore
17. Tripura's literacy rate in 2011 was approximately:
18. Which state borders Tripura on the east?
(a) Assam and Mizoram  (b) Nagaland and Manipur  (c) Meghalaya only  (d) Manipur only
19. Tripura High Court was established in:
20. The Tripura Legislative Assembly has how many seats?
21. Tripura has how many Lok Sabha constituencies:

(a) They came from Myanmar  (b) They came from Bangladesh  (c) They fled ethnic violence in Mizoram and settled in North Tripura for 23+ years before being permanently settled in 2020  (d) They came from Tibet
23. Neermahal (Water Palace) is located on:
(a) Dumbur Lake  (b) Rudrasagar Lake  (c) Gomati River  (d) Howrah River
24. Neermahal was built by which Maharaja:
(a) Bir Chandra Manikya  (b) Radha Kishore Manikya  (c) Bir Bikram Kishore Manikya  (d) Kirit Bikram Kishore
25. Tripura's Hojagiri dance received UNESCO recognition in:

(a) Tripuri  (b) Jamatia  (c) Reang (Bru)  (d) Chakma
27. The Kokborok language is spoken by which tribe:
(a) Reang  (b) Tripuri (Twipra)  (c) Chakma  (d) Mog
28. Who among the following is a famous music director born in Agartala, Tripura:
(a) A.R. Rahman  (b) R.D. Burman  (c) Sachin Dev Burman (S.D. Burman)  (d) Laxmikant

(a) Direct war with Pakistan  (b) Being surrounded by Pakistan/Bangladesh on three sides; massive refugee influx changing demographics  (c) Loss of sea port  (d) Division of Tripura territory

(a) One  (b) Two  (c) Three  (d) Four

(a) Vedic period only  (b) Buddhist and Hindu (8th–12th century CE)  (c) Mughal period  (d) British colonial period
Section B — Geography, Biodiversity & Environment (Q36–Q70)

(a) Smallest  (b) Second smallest  (c) Third smallest  (d) Fourth smallest
37. The highest peak in Tripura is:
(a) Sakhan Hills  (b) Atharamura Peak  (c) Betlingchip (939 m) in Jampui Hills  (d) Longtarai Peak
38. The state animal of Tripura is:
(a) Elephant  (b) Phayre's Langur  (c) Clouded Leopard  (d) Gaur
39. The state bird of Tripura is:

(a) Great Hornbill  (b) Green Imperial Pigeon  (c) Peacock  (d) Blood Pheasant

(a) Rubber tree  (b) Hollong  (c) Agar (Aquilaria malaccensis)  (d) Teak
41. Agarwood (Oud) is obtained from which tree (state tree of Tripura):
(a) Sandalwood  (b) Agar / Aquilaria malaccensis  (c) Khair (Acacia catechu)  (d) Rosewood
42. Dumbur Lake (Rudrasagar reservoir) is on which river:
(a) Howrah  (b) Manu  (c) Gumti (Gomati)  (d) Khowai

(a) Howrah  (b) Manu  (c) Gumti (Gomati) — ~160 km  (d) Khowai

(a) Elephant  (b) Clouded Leopard  (c) Phayre's Langur (state animal)  (d) Gaur
45. Sepahijala Wildlife Sanctuary is known for:
(a) Wild elephant herds  (b) Clouded Leopard and Spectacled Monkey (Phayre's Langur)  (c) Tiger reserve  (d) Migratory bird sanctuary
46. The Jampui Hills in North Tripura are known as the '___ of Tripura':
(a) Valley of Flowers  (b) Switzerland  (c) Queen of Hills  (d) Orange Valley
47. Which geological feature explains the presence of natural gas in Tripura:
(a) Volcanic activity  (b) Tripura Folds (folded anticlines and synclines)  (c) Alluvial deposits  (d) Deccan Traps
48. Tripura shares a boundary of approximately ___ km with Bangladesh:
49. The Rudrasagar Lake (with Neermahal) is in which district:
(a) Dhalai  (b) North Tripura  (c) South Tripura (near Udaipur)  (d) West Tripura
50. The Palatana Gas Power Project (726.6 MW) is in which district:
(a) West Tripura  (b) North Tripura  (c) Gomati  (d) South Tripura (Udaipur)
51. Tripura's forest cover is approximately what percentage of its total area:
52. The state flower of Tripura is:
(a) Lotus  (b) Nageshwar (Mesua ferrea / Indian Rose Chestnut)  (c) Orchid  (d) Rhododendron
53. Which district of Tripura borders only Assam (not Bangladesh):
(a) Unokoti  (b) West Tripura  (c) South Tripura  (d) Dhalai
54. Rowa Wildlife Sanctuary, smallest in Tripura, is primarily:
(a) Elephant reserve  (b) Botanical/Plant reserve  (c) Tiger corridor  (d) Migratory bird site
55. The Tripura Sundari temple (one of 51 Shakti Peethas) is in:
(a) Agartala  (b) Udaipur (South Tripura)  (c) Kailashahar  (d) Ambassa
56. The climate of Tripura is best described as:
(a) Semi-arid  (b) Humid tropical monsoon  (c) Alpine  (d) Mediterranean
57. Tripura receives average annual rainfall of approximately:
58. The Howrah River flows through which city of Tripura:
(a) Udaipur  (b) Dharmanagar  (c) Agartala  (d) Ambassa
59. Tripura is India's ___ largest natural rubber producer:
(a) 1st  (b) 2nd  (c) 3rd  (d) 4th
60. The Dumbur Hydroelectric Project (40 MW) is on which river in Dhalai district:
(a) Manu  (b) Gumti (Gomati)  (c) Khowai  (d) Longai
61. Unokoti district of Tripura is the ___ smallest district in India:
(a) Largest in Tripura  (b) Smallest district in Tripura  (c) Second smallest in Tripura  (d) Medium-sized
62. The Gumti Wildlife Sanctuary is important primarily for:
(a) Clouded Leopard  (b) Wild Elephant conservation and elephant corridor  (c) Tiger conservation  (d) Bird sanctuary
63. Tripura's natural gas is particularly important for which sector:
(a) Automobile fuel  (b) Power generation; OTPC Palatana plant and other uses  (c) Plastic manufacturing only  (d) Aviation fuel
64. The Queen variety of which fruit from Tripura has received GI tag:
(a) Orange  (b) Jackfruit  (c) Pineapple  (d) Banana
65. Betlingchip peak (939 m) is the highest point in Tripura. It is in:
(a) Longtarai Hills  (b) Sakhan Hills  (c) Jampui Hills, North Tripura  (d) Atharamura Hills
66. The Clouded Leopard captive breeding programme in Tripura is at:
(a) Gumti WLS  (b) Trishna WLS  (c) Sipahijola Zoo (Sepahijala)  (d) Rowa WLS
67. Tripura's Agarwood (Oud) is internationally traded and regulated under:
(a) WTO trade rules  (b) CITES (Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species)  (c) Paris Agreement  (d) CBD (Convention on Biological Diversity)
68. Tripura's approximate area is:
(a) 5,000 sq km  (b) 8,000 sq km  (c) 10,486 sq km  (d) 15,000 sq km
69. The Manu River is important for which district:
(a) South Tripura  (b) Dhalai  (c) North Tripura and Unokoti  (d) West Tripura
70. Which river flows past Agartala, the capital of Tripura:
(a) Gumti  (b) Howrah  (c) Manu  (d) Khowai
Section C — Economy, Culture & Current Affairs (Q71–Q100)
71. Tripura's literacy rate (87.75%) ranks ___ in India:
(a) 1st  (b) 2nd  (c) 3rd  (d) 4th
72. Which is the most important festival of the Tripuri tribe, worshipping the god of prosperity:
(a) Ker Puja  (b) Kharchi Puja  (c) Garia Puja  (d) Durga Puja
73. Kokborok is:
(a) A dance form of Tripura  (b) The tribal language of the Tripuri people; one of two official languages of Tripura  (c) A type of bamboo handicraft  (d) A species of bamboo
74. Tripura is India's second largest producer of:
(a) Tea  (b) Bamboo  (c) Natural rubber  (d) Agarwood
75. Agarbatti (incense sticks) production in Tripura primarily uses:
(a) Wood pulp  (b) Bamboo sticks  (c) Sugarcane fibres  (d) Plastic tubes
76. Dipa Karmakar from Agartala became famous for:
(a) Swimming at Olympics  (b) Being the first Indian woman gymnast to compete at Olympics (Rio 2016)  (c) Winning gold in Asian Games badminton  (d) First Indian to win gymnastics World Championship
77. The Rignai cloth of the Tripuri tribe has received:
(a) Nobel Prize recognition  (b) GI (Geographical Indication) tag  (c) UNESCO inscription  (d) National Award from ASI
78. Which is the only floating palace in northeast India:
(a) Ujjayanta Palace  (b) Neermahal (Water Palace) on Rudrasagar Lake  (c) Rabindra Bhavan  (d) Rajbari Palace
79. The Ujjayanta Palace in Agartala was built by:
(a) Bir Chandra Manikya  (b) Radha Kishore Manikya (1901)  (c) Bir Bikram Kishore  (d) Dhanya Manikya
80. S.D. Burman (Sachin Dev Burman), born in Agartala, was associated with:
(a) Classical Carnatic music  (b) Bollywood / Hindi film music composition  (c) Classical Hindustani music only  (d) Bengali Baul music
81. The Akhaura-Agartala Rail Link was inaugurated in:
(a) November 2021  (b) March 2023  (c) November 2023  (d) January 2024
82. The Maitri Setu (Feni River bridge at Sabroom) is significant because:
(a) It connects Tripura to Assam  (b) It connects Tripura's Sabroom to Bangladesh's Ramgarh; gives access to Chittagong Port  (c) It is India's longest cable bridge  (d) It connects India to Myanmar
83. The historic Agartala to Kolkata distance via Bangladesh (by rail) is approximately:
84. TIPRA Motha won how many seats in the 2023 Tripura election:

items: Questions 1 to 35 test foundational concepts in History, Polity, and Indian Governance.
Questions 36 to 70 focus heavily on environmental policies, physical geography, and biodiversity conservation.
Questions 71 to 100 evaluate economic principles, Indian culture, and contemporary current affairs.

blocks.content: 85. The Bru-Reang refugees lived in relief camps in North Tripura for approximately:
(a) 5 years  (b) 10 years  (c) 15 years  (d) 23+ years (1997–2020)
86. Which Tripura festival was included in UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2023:
(a) Kharchi Puja  (b) Garia Puja  (c) Hojagiri dance of the Reang tribe  (d) Ker Puja
87. The OTPC Palatana power plant in Tripura is based on:
(a) Coal  (b) Hydropower  (c) Natural gas  (d) Solar power
88. The NIT Agartala (National Institute of Technology) was originally established as:
(a) IIT Agartala  (b) Tripura Engineering College (1965)  (c) Tripura University Engineering Department  (d) NE Technical School
89. The 'Greater Tipraland' demand by TIPRA Motha seeks:

(a) A separate national capital for tribals  (b) Constitutional protection and possibly a separate state for tribal communities of Tripura  (c) Merger of Tripura with Bangladesh  (d) Special economic zone for Tripura
90. Orange Festival in Tripura is held in which area:
(a) Agartala  (b) Jampui Hills, North Tripura  (c) Udaipur  (d) Ambassa
91. Tripura Central University (full name: Tripura University) is located at:
(a) Agartala city centre  (b) Suryamaninagar, Agartala  (c) Udaipur  (d) Dharmanagar
92. The Rubber Park in Tripura is at:
(a) Agartala  (b) Bodhjungnagar, West Tripura  (c) Sabroom  (d) Kailashahar
93. Which ancient site in Tripura has Buddhist and Hindu sculptures dating to 8th–12th century CE:
(a) Unakoti  (b) Pilak (South Tripura)  (c) Old Agartala  (d) Udaipur fort
94. The Maharaja Bir Bikram Airport (Agartala airport) is the ___ busiest airport in northeast India:
(a) 1st (busiest)  (b) 2nd (after Guwahati)  (c) 3rd  (d) 4th
95. The Ashokastami Mela is held at which Tripura site annually:
(a) Tripura Sundari Temple, Udaipur  (b) Unakoti  (c) Old Agartala Temple  (d) Neermahal
96. Tripura's state sport is:
(a) Kabaddi  (b) Football  (c) Gilla Danda  (d) Wrestling
97. The Chakma tribe of Tripura follows which religion:
(a) Hinduism  (b) Theravada Buddhism  (c) Christianity  (d) Donyi-Polo
98. Under the Bru-Reang settlement agreement (2020), each displaced family receives how much cash:
(a) Rs 50,000  (b) Rs 1 lakh  (c) Rs 1.5 lakh  (d) Rs 5 lakh
99. The Gumti (Gomati) River ultimately flows into:
(a) Brahmaputra  (b) Barak River  (c) Bangladesh (Meghna river system)  (d) Bay of Bengal directly
100. Tripura's Queen Pineapple GI tag was awarded — Tripura ranks approximately ___ in pineapple production in India:
(a) 1st  (b) 2nd  (c) 3rd  (d) 5th
